# Results -- Study 510 (Frog-In-The-Pan) on real yfinance panel

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Protocol: 12-1 cross-sectional
momentum double-sorted with the Da-Gurun-Warachka **information-discreteness (ID)** measure;
the LOW-ID (gradual / Frog-In-The-Pan) winners-minus-losers (WML) book raced against the
HIGH-ID (discrete) WML book, with the FIP interaction (low minus high), a label-shuffle
placebo, one execution lag, costs and short borrow, on a large-cap S&P 500 survivor basket.
As-of **2026-06-26**.*

## The verdict, earned -- Signal `NONE` · Tradability `MIRAGE` · "Does gradual beat jumpy?" `MIXED`

Da, Gurun & Warachka (2014) argue momentum is concentrated in stocks whose past return arrived
**gradually** (low information-discreteness) -- a frog boiled slowly never jumps out of the pan,
and neither does the under-reacting market. On this 38-name large-cap survivor basket the
*direction* shows up (the LOW-ID WML out-earns the HIGH-ID WML by **+4.55%/yr**) but the
interaction's HAC *t* is **+1.01** -- below the |t| >= 2 bar -- and the LOW-ID book that is
supposed to carry the premium earns **-0.37%/yr** at *t* = **-0.09**, statistically zero. The
label-shuffle placebo confirms it: **p = 0.56** (seed-robust 0.54-0.57), the real LOW-ID mean
sits *below* its own shuffled null. Net of 5 bps/leg + 50 bps/yr borrow the LOW-ID book is
**-1.29%/yr**. So `NONE` on the signal (no FIP premium clears the bar), `MIRAGE` on tradability
(the gradual book is negative net of costs), and `MIXED` on the qualitative "does gradual beat
jumpy?" -- the sign is right (and the synthetic control proves the engine would catch it if it
were there) but the magnitude is statistically indistinguishable from zero on this tape.

## Data stamp

| Frame | Shape | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| Prices (daily adjusted-close) | 3424 days × 38 tickers | `e038fa42cc02` |
| Period covered | 2012-05-18 -- 2025-12-30 | -- |
| Monthly month-ends | 164 | -- |
| Stamped WML months | 151 (2013 -- 2025) | -- |

**Source:** yfinance daily adjusted-close prices (auto_adjust=True). Basket: 38 large-cap
S&P 500 names (after coverage filtering from a 40-name candidate list). The partial current
month is dropped; the stamped run contains only completed months.

**Survivorship bias (named on the SIGNAL axis, not just tradability):** the basket is current
large-caps projected backwards. A *gradual* decline into delisting is precisely a LOW-ID loser,
so the names that would most strengthen the FIP short leg -- firms that drifted quietly to zero
-- are systematically absent. The LOW-ID slice is therefore the **more inflated** of the two,
and all positive numbers here are **upper-bound estimates**. Opt-in guard: feed
[`strategy.long_short`](../frog_in_the_pan/strategy.py) a delisting-complete panel to lift the
bias; yfinance cannot supply one, so we flag it rather than hide it.

## The honest test -- momentum double-sorted on information-discreteness

The 12-1 momentum signal (trailing 12 months, skip the most recent month) and the ID measure
`ID = sign(PRET) · (%neg − %pos)` are both computed at each month-end *t* from prices up to and
including *t*; the book is entered one trading day later and earns month *t+1* (one forward lag,
no same-bar fill). Each month the cross-section is split at its median ID; inside the chosen half
the top/bottom 30% by momentum form a dollar-neutral WML book.

| Book | N mo | Mean (ann) | Vol | Sharpe | **HAC t** | Hit | Max-DD |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Plain momentum WML (no ID split) | 151 | **+0.18%/yr** | 13.9% | +0.01 | **+0.05** | 53.0% | −30.9% |
| **LOW-ID** (gradual / FIP) WML | 151 | **−0.37%/yr** | 15.6% | −0.02 | **−0.09** | 54.3% | −43.4% |
| **HIGH-ID** (discrete) WML | 151 | **−4.92%/yr** | 13.3% | −0.37 | **−1.32** | 50.3% | −56.9% |
| **FIP interaction** (LOW − HIGH) | 151 | **+4.55%/yr** | — | — | **+1.01** | 57.6% | — |

- Plain momentum is **dead** on this large-cap survivor basket (+0.18%/yr, *t* 0.05) -- the
  familiar large-cap-momentum flatness this desk records in [24 Stampede](../../24-stampede/)
  and [507 Cross-Sectional-Momentum](../../507-cross-sectional-momentum/).
- The LOW-ID (gradual) slice is supposed to *carry* the premium. It does not: **−0.37%/yr**,
  HAC *t* = **−0.09** -- statistically zero, and *worse* than the plain book.
- The HIGH-ID (discrete) slice is the more negative (−4.92%/yr), so the **interaction is
  positive** (+4.55%/yr): gradual does beat jumpy, as the theory says. But the interaction's
  HAC *t* is only **+1.01** -- the direction is right, the significance is not there.

## Costs -- the LOW-ID book is negative net

| Charge | Value |
|---|---|
| One-way cost | 5 bps/leg per rebalance |
| Short borrow | 50 bps/yr on the loser leg |
| Avg turnover | 35.0%/mo (avg 6 names/leg) |
| LOW-ID WML, **gross** | −0.37%/yr (*t* −0.09) |
| LOW-ID WML, **net** | **−1.29%/yr** (*t* −0.31, Sharpe −0.08) |

Even before costs the gradual book is flat-to-negative; costs and borrow only deepen the hole.
There is nothing to monetise.

## Robustness -- the placebo agrees there is no edge

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Label-shuffle placebo p (LOW-ID, 1000 perms) | **0.558** |
| Real LOW-ID mean vs shuffled null | real −0.37%/yr **below** placebo mean +0.18%/yr |
| Seed-robustness of p (seeds 1/7/42/510/2024) | 0.550 / 0.545 / 0.540 / 0.573 / 0.547 |

Shuffling which stock the momentum signal points at (inside the LOW-ID half) destroys any genuine
winner/loser persistence. The real mean lands *below* the centre of the shuffled distribution:
**p = 0.56**, stable across five RNG seeds. A real edge would give a small p; this gives p ≈ 0.5.
There is no FIP momentum premium here to shuffle away.

## Synthetic positive control -- the engine is faithful (NOT a real-tape claim)

A deterministic panel where the planted drift is delivered *smoothly* to the low-ID half and in
*jumps* to the high-ID half. The engine must score ~0 at strength 0 and recover a LARGER low-ID
WML than high-ID WML as the planted drift grows.

| Planted strength | LOW-ID WML (ann) | LOW-ID t | HIGH-ID WML (ann) | HIGH-ID t | FIP gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.00 (null) | −0.5% | −0.09 | +4.4% | +0.95 | −4.8% |
| 0.20 | +13.6% | +2.60 | +12.2% | +2.13 | +1.4% |
| 0.40 | +40.2% | +6.98 | +28.9% | +4.74 | +11.3% |
| 0.60 | +77.2% | +9.87 | +38.0% | +5.99 | +39.2% |

The engine recovers a positive, monotone FIP gap when the effect is *planted* (and scores ~0 at
the null). So the flat real-tape result reflects **the market**, not a broken detector. This is a
power check only -- never cited to support the real-tape stamp.

A coin-flip of up and down years with no persistent drift -- the signature of a non-signal.

## The honest takeaway

The Frog-In-The-Pan *idea* is real and elegant, and the *direction* survives on this tape:
gradual (low-ID) momentum out-earns jumpy (high-ID) momentum by +4.55%/yr. But on a 38-name
large-cap survivor basket the interaction clears nothing (HAC *t* +1.01), the gradual book that
should carry the premium is statistically zero (−0.37%/yr, *t* −0.09) and negative net of costs
(−1.29%/yr), and a seed-robust label-shuffle places the real mean *below* its own null (p 0.56).
`NONE` on the signal, `MIRAGE` on tradability, `MIXED` on "does gradual beat jumpy?" -- the sign
is on the theory's side, the significance is not, and the survivorship bias cuts the FIP slice's
way. A pointed academic factor, replicated honestly on a thin survivor basket, lands exactly
where the desk expects.
